sections.content:
94,450 people

were counted on the census as "bar staff" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Bar staff prepare, mix and serve alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks and beverages at bars in public houses, hotels, clubs and other establishments.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "bar staff" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "bar staff", 37.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "bar staff" was 65 years or older.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "bar staff" included:

  • sports and leisure assistants
  • waiters and waitresses
  • coffee shop workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "bar staff" there were more women than men (57.3% compared with 42.7%).

This means "bar staff" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 42.7% and women made up 57.3% of "bar staff"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "bar staff" included:

  • customer service managers
  • elementary administration occupations (other)
  • national government administrative occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "bar staff" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "bar staff" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "bar staff", 14% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (77.7% compared with 22.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.6%) than self-employed (1.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
